name: Crete
note: Europa to Minos, and the house of the labyrinth

Pasiphae.note: Daughter of Helios, wife of Minos, and mother of the Minotaur by the white bull -- Poseidon's punishment on her husband, worked out on her. Apollod. 3.1.2-4

Europa.note: Carried off from the Phoenician shore by Zeus in the shape of a white bull, and set down in Crete. A continent is named for her, and nobody is sure why -- the name may be Semitic, ereb, the west, the same root that stands behind Erebos. Apollod. 3.1.1

Minos.note: King of Knossos and the first sea-power; he demanded seven youths and seven maidens from Athens every ninth year for the labyrinth. A judge of the dead afterwards. Arthur Evans named the whole MINOAN civilisation after him in 1900. Apollod. 3.1.1-4

Rhadamanthys.note: Brother of Minos, so just a lawgiver that he became the second judge of the dead beside him and Aiakos. Apollod. 3.1.2

Sarpedon.note: Brother of Minos; the name passes to his descendant, the Lykian king Zeus watches die at Troy and cannot save, because not even Zeus overturns what is fated. Il. 16.419-505

Minotauros.name: Minotauros (Minotaur)
Minotauros.note: Asterios, the bull of Minos: born to Pasiphae by the white bull Poseidon sent when Minos would not sacrifice it, and shut in the labyrinth Daidalos built. Apollod. 3.1.4

Ariadne.note: Gave Theseus the ball of thread that got him out, sailed with him, and was left asleep on Naxos -- where Dionysos found her and married her, and her crown is a constellation. Apollod. Epit. 1.8-9

Phaidra.name: Phaidra (Phaedra)
Phaidra.note: Her sister, married to Theseus, who fell in love with her stepson and hanged herself leaving a letter accusing him. Euripides Hippolytus

people.Androgeos: Son of Minos, killed at Athens, and the reason for the tribute of youths. Apollod. 3.15.7

Deukalion2.name: Deukalion
Deukalion2.note: Son of Minos, and father of Idomeneus. Not Deukalion of the flood. Apollod. 3.3.1

Idomeneus.note: King of Crete at Troy, who led eighty ships and vowed to sacrifice the first thing he met at home. Il. 2.645-652

unions.note: By Zeus in Crete after the bull set her down. Apollod. 3.1.1
By the bull. A one-parent union, because the other parent is not a person. Apollod. 3.1.4
Carried off from the Phoenician shore on the back of a white bull and set down in Crete. Apollod. 3.1.1
